did_you_know.text: The title identifies the passage as “A psalm of David” and dedicates it to the chief musician.
The king is described as rejoicing in the LORD’s strength and salvation, and as being exceedingly glad.
The verse says that the LORD granted both the king’s heart’s desire and his requests, called “the request of his lips.”
Good blessings are described as going before the king, and a “crown of pure gold” is placed on his head.
The king asked for life, and the verse describes his request being granted with the words “length of days, forever and ever.”
The LORD’s salvation gives the king great glory, majesty, and splendor; in other words, salvation is also portrayed as a source of status and honor.
The blessings upon the king are described as lasting forever, and his joy is connected to the LORD’s presence: “You make him glad with the joy of your presence.”
At the heart of the description of the king’s stability is his trust in the LORD; according to the verse, the steadfast love of the Most High keeps him from being shaken.
The judgment of the enemies includes an image of intense fire: they are compared to a fiery furnace, and the verse attributes their destruction to the LORD’s wrath.
The conclusion asks the LORD to rise up in his strength and ends with a commitment to sing and praise his power.
